import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/training_3.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_23_0 and Source3_23_1 on "Wrestler"
join_01 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="Wrestler", suffixes=('_0', '_1'), how='outer')

# Operation 2: JOIN Source3_23_2 and Source3_23_3 on "Wrestler"
join_23 = pd.merge(df2, df3, on="Wrestler", suffixes=('_2', '_3'), how='outer')

# Operation 3: GROUP BY Source3_23_0.Wrestler (which is the same as join keys "Wrestler")
# Aggregations: sum of Wins, Losses, Draws from each joined dataframe part
# Because join_01 and join_23 are separate, we need to join them on Wrestler to aggregate all sums together

# First, aggregate sums on join_01
agg_01 = join_01.groupby("Wrestler", as_index=False).agg({
    'Wins_0': 'sum',
    'Losses_0': 'sum',
    'Draws_0': 'sum',
    'Wins_1': 'sum',
    'Losses_1': 'sum',
    'Draws_1': 'sum'
})

# Aggregate sums on join_23
agg_23 = join_23.groupby("Wrestler", as_index=False).agg({
    'Wins_2': 'sum',
    'Losses_2': 'sum',
    'Draws_2': 'sum',
    'Wins_3': 'sum',
    'Losses_3': 'sum',
    'Draws_3': 'sum'
})

# Join the two aggregated results on Wrestler to combine all sums
agg_all = pd.merge(agg_01, agg_23, on="Wrestler", how='outer')

# Fill NaN with 0 for aggregation columns (in case some Wrestlers appear only in one side)
agg_all.fillna(0, inplace=True)

# Operation 4: PIVOT
# The target schema has columns for years 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 with Wins, Losses, Draws each.
# From the source naming and suffixes, we can map:
# Source3_23_0 -> 2013
# Source3_23_1 -> 2014
# Source3_23_2 -> 2015
# Source3_23_3 -> 2016

# Rename columns accordingly to match target schema
agg_all.rename(columns={
    'Wins_0': '2013 Wins',
    'Losses_0': '2013 Losses',
    'Draws_0': '2013 Draws',
    'Wins_1': '2014 Wins',
    'Losses_1': '2014 Losses',
    'Draws_1': '2014 Draws',
    'Wins_2': '2015 Wins',
    'Losses_2': '2015 Losses',
    'Draws_2': '2015 Draws',
    'Wins_3': '2016 Wins',
    'Losses_3': '2016 Losses',
    'Draws_3': '2016 Draws'
}, inplace=True)

# Ensure integer type for all count columns as per target schema
count_columns = [
    '2013 Wins', '2013 Losses', '2013 Draws',
    '2014 Wins', '2014 Losses', '2014 Draws',
    '2015 Wins', '2015 Losses', '2015 Draws',
    '2016 Wins', '2016 Losses', '2016 Draws'
]
agg_all[count_columns] = agg_all[count_columns].astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema order
final_columns = ['Wrestler'] + count_columns
target_df = agg_all[final_columns]

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
s0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
s1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
s2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
s3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Rename columns in each source to match target year columns
# Source 0 -> 2013 columns
s0 = s0.rename(columns={
    'Wins': '2013 Wins',
    'Losses': '2013 Losses',
    'Draws': '2013 Draws'
})

# Source 1 -> 2014 columns
s1 = s1.rename(columns={
    'Wins': '2014 Wins',
    'Losses': '2014 Losses',
    'Draws': '2014 Draws'
})

# Source 2 -> 2015 columns
s2 = s2.rename(columns={
    'Wins': '2015 Wins',
    'Losses': '2015 Losses',
    'Draws': '2015 Draws'
})

# Source 3 -> 2016 columns
s3 = s3.rename(columns={
    'Wins': '2016 Wins',
    'Losses': '2016 Losses',
    'Draws': '2016 Draws'
})

# Join Source0 and Source1 on Wrestler (inner join)
join_01 = pd.merge(s0, s1, on='Wrestler', how='inner')

# Join Source2 and Source3 on Wrestler (inner join)
join_23 = pd.merge(s2, s3, on='Wrestler', how='inner')

# Join the two joined tables on Wrestler (inner join)
joined_all = pd.merge(join_01, join_23, on='Wrestler', how='inner')

# Group by Wrestler and sum all numeric columns (to handle duplicates if any)
result = joined_all.groupby('Wrestler', as_index=False).sum()

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = ['Wrestler',
                  '2013 Wins', '2013 Losses', '2013 Draws',
                  '2014 Wins', '2014 Losses', '2014 Draws',
                  '2015 Wins', '2015 Losses', '2015 Draws',
                  '2016 Wins', '2016 Losses', '2016 Draws']

result = result[target_columns]

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_23/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
